```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment="#>")
library("coherentSurv")
```

## Specify the complete support

The finite-path interface observes a baseline stratum for everyone and a complete
path only for recorded subjects. This is a whole-path recording experiment,
not the same observation model as right censoring. Here two windows have marks
zero (no event), one and two (recurrent types), and three (terminal event).
Absorption leaves thirteen legal paths.

```{r support}
paths <- as.matrix(expand.grid(second=0:3, first=0:2)[,c("first","second")])
paths <- rbind(paths,c(3,NA))
features <- cbind(count1=rowSums(paths==1,na.rm=TRUE),
                  count2=rowSums(paths==2,na.rm=TRUE),
                  terminal=as.numeric(rowSums(paths==3,na.rm=TRUE)>0),
                  grid_alive=1+as.numeric(paths[,1]!=3))
features
```

The fourth target is restricted survival on this two-window grid; it is not a
continuous-time restricted mean without further modelling.

## Fit nuisances in training folds and evaluate influence functions

```{r targeting}
set.seed(104)
n <- 800
strata <- rep(0:1,length.out=n)
path <- sample(seq_len(nrow(features)),n,replace=TRUE)
recorded <- rbinom(n,1,.8-.3*strata)
path[recorded==0] <- NA
folds <- sample(rep(1:5,length.out=n))
target <- cs_target(path,recorded,strata,features,folds=folds)
data.frame(target=names(target$estimate),estimate=target$estimate,
           se=target$se,EIF_mean=target$EIF_mean,
           EIF_variance=target$EIF_variance)
target$convergence
```

The estimator uses training-fold path and recording probabilities and a common
exponential tilt. The individual efficient influence function (EIF) combines a
regression prediction with a recording-weighted residual. Missing paths are
never read. The output retains folds, nuisances, updated laws and score residuals.
MAR conditional on the stratum and recording positivity identify these targets.
Efficiency further requires regularity and nuisance-rate conditions; a small
empirical EIF mean alone does not prove efficiency.

## Replace point identification with a declared sensitivity region

This separate example has three complete atoms, known recording fraction 0.7,
and a terminal indicator on the third atom. The parameter `kappa` bounds the
relative odds of missing versus recorded mass. Its unit value supplies the
random-recording boundary for this finite model.

```{r bounds}
counts <- c(50,30,20)
results <- lapply(c(1,2,4),function(k) {
  b <- cs_bounds(counts/sum(counts),c(0,0,1),kappa=k,
                 recording_fraction=.7,counts=counts)
  data.frame(kappa=k,lower=b$lower,upper=b$upper,
             confidence_lower=b$outer$lower,
             confidence_upper=b$outer$upper)
})
do.call(rbind,results)
```

The plug-in bounds describe identification uncertainty. The outer confidence
limits additionally account for multinomial sampling through simultaneous
Clopper-Pearson constraints. The linear programs use recorded-law constraints,
not EIF scores. This distinction preserves the assumptions of both procedures.
An unknown recording fraction requires a different model or a separately
specified sensitivity analysis.

## Rounded dates require legal path integration

`cs_colon()` builds an explicit day-coarsening experiment from the public
`survival` dataset. A recorded recurrence and death on the same day permits
recurrence before death inside that day. It does not permit omitting the
documented recurrence. Four and eight quadrature nodes can be compared.
The adapter loads data from its source package rather than bundling patient rows.

```{r colon, eval=FALSE}
a <- cs_colon(nodes=4,covariate="node4")
fit <- cs_fit(a$formula,a$data,event_types=a$event_types,
                 nonrecurrent=a$nonrecurrent,time_unit="years",
                 breaks=c(0,1,3,Inf),observation="coarsened",
                 coarsening=a$coarsening)
```

For a coarsened forecast at a landmark, construct compatible past paths ending
at that landmark and call `cs_predict_paths()`. Passing full-follow-up paths
would disclose future outcomes and is rejected. Each legal past retains its
own posterior gamma component; the mixture is averaged after propagation.
